config.title: Scope, Hoisting & the TDZ

intro.title: Scope, Hoisting & the TDZ
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple program that demonstrates how JavaScript handles variable declarations and function definitions before your code runs. You will learn the core concepts of scope, which defines where variables are accessible, hoisting, which moves declarations to the top of their scope, and the Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ), which restricts access to variables before they are declared. The main technologies involved are JavaScript's var, let, const declarations and function definitions. By the end, you'll understand how these mechanisms affect your code's behavior and how to avoid common pitfalls.
intro.usecase: Understanding scope, hoisting, and the Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ) is essential for writing bug-free JavaScript in real-world applications like interactive dashboards and forms. For example, when building a dynamic dashboard that updates charts based on user filters, misusing variable scope can lead to data leaks or errors where filter variables are accessed before initialization. In complex forms with conditional fields, hoisting rules determine whether validation functions are available when the form loads, preventing runtime errors. Mastering these concepts helps developers avoid subtle bugs in UI components like modals or data tables, ensuring reliable and maintainable code.

objectives: Apply variable scope rules to control data accessibility in different code blocks
Construct functions that demonstrate lexical scope and closure behavior
Manipulate variable declarations to observe hoisting effects in execution
Initialize variables within the Temporal Dead Zone to trigger reference errors
Configure code examples that differentiate between var, let, and const hoisting
Implement practical solutions to avoid common scope-related bugs
Update existing code to resolve Temporal Dead Zone issues

steps.title: Create a JavaScript file and define global scope variables
steps.instruction: Create a new JavaScript file and declare three variables in the global scope: one using 'var', one using 'let', and one using 'const'.
steps.hint: Start by declaring a variable with 'var', then another with 'let', and finally one with 'const'. Give each variable a different name and assign them initial values.
steps.expectedOutcome: Three variables declared in the global scope using different declaration keywords.
successCriteria: Variables are declared in the global scope using var, let, and const keywords with valid names and initial values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've declared some variables, but make sure you have one using var, one using let, and one using const in the global scope.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to declare three variables in the global scope: one with var, one with let, and one with const.

steps.title: Create a function to demonstrate function scope
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'demonstrateFunctionScope' that will contain variables declared with different keywords to show how function scope works.
steps.hint: Define a function using either 'function demonstrateFunctionScope() {}' or 'const demonstrateFunctionScope = () => {}'.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a function named 'demonstrateFunctionScope' defined in your code.
successCriteria: A function named 'demonstrateFunctionScope' is created with a function body (can be empty or contain placeholder code).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've created a function with the exact name 'demonstrateFunctionScope'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function wasn't created correctly. Check that you used the correct name and proper function syntax.

steps.title: Create a block scope with let and const
steps.instruction: Create a block using curly braces {} and inside it, declare two variables: one with let and one with const.
steps.hint: You can create a block by simply writing a pair of curly braces. Inside those braces, use let and const to declare variables.
steps.expectedOutcome: A block scope is created with let and const variables inside it, demonstrating that these variables are confined to the block.
successCriteria: A block is created using curly braces, containing a let variable declaration and a const variable declaration inside it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've created a block using curly braces and declared both a let and a const variable inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a block using curly braces {} and inside it, declare one variable with let and another with const.

steps.title: Demonstrate hoisting with var declarations
steps.instruction: Write a console.log statement that accesses the globalVar variable before its declaration line to demonstrate hoisting behavior.
steps.hint: Place your console.log statement above the line where globalVar is declared. Use the variable name without any let or const keywords.
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will run without throwing an error, and console.log will output 'undefined' because var declarations are hoisted but not initialized.
successCriteria: A console.log statement is placed before the var declaration that accesses globalVar, demonstrating hoisting behavior.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're accessing globalVar before its declaration line, and using console.log to output it.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're writing a console.log statement that accesses globalVar before it's declared in the code.

steps.title: Demonstrate hoisting with function declarations
steps.instruction: Call a function named 'hoistedFunction' before its declaration in your code to demonstrate function hoisting.
steps.hint: Place a function call (e.g., hoistedFunction();) above where the function is defined.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function 'hoistedFunction' is called before it is declared, demonstrating that function declarations are hoisted to the top of their scope.
successCriteria: A function call to 'hoistedFunction' appears before the function's declaration in the code.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling a function named 'hoistedFunction' before it's defined.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the instruction: you need to call a function named 'hoistedFunction' before its declaration to show hoisting.

steps.title: Show that let/const are hoisted but not initialized
steps.instruction: Add a console.log statement that attempts to access a let variable before its declaration to demonstrate the Temporal Dead Zone error.
steps.hint: Place a console.log statement above the variable declaration that tries to log the variable's value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will throw a ReferenceError when trying to access a let variable before its declaration, demonstrating the Temporal Dead Zone.
successCriteria: A console.log statement attempts to access a let variable before its declaration, showing TDZ behavior.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're trying to access a let variable before its declaration to properly demonstrate TDZ.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add a console.log statement that attempts to access a let variable before it's declared to show the Temporal Dead Zone error.

steps.title: Create a TDZ scenario with block scope
steps.instruction: Create nested blocks and attempt to access variables in TDZ across different scopes. Add an outer block with a let variable,
steps.hint: Start with an outer block using curly braces {}. Inside it, add a console.log statement that tries to access a variable before declaring it with let in the same outer block.
steps.expectedOutcome: The learner will create nested blocks where a variable is accessed in the Temporal Dead Zone before its declaration, demonstrating how TDZ works within block scopes.
successCriteria: Nested blocks are created with an outer block containing a console.log that attempts to access a variable before its let declaration in the same block.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created blocks, but make sure you have an outer block with a console.log that tries to access a variable before declaring it with let in the same block.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the structure: you need nested blocks where the outer block contains a console.log statement attempting to use a variable before its let declaration.

steps.title: Demonstrate function expressions vs declarations i
steps.instruction: Create a function declaration and a function expression,
steps.hint: Define a function declaration (e.g., function myDeclaration() {}) and a function expression (e.g., const myExpression = function() {}). Then, add calls to both functions above their definitions.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will see that the function declaration works when called before its definition due to hoisting, while the function expression throws an error because it is not hoisted.
successCriteria: A function declaration and a function expression are defined, and both are called before their definitions in the code.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both a function declaration and a function expression, and that you call them before their definitions.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've created both a function declaration and a function expression, and called them before their definitions. Review hoisting differences between declarations and expressions.

steps.title: Create a practical example showing scope chain
steps.instruction: Create a function named outerFunction that declares a variable 'outerVar' with the value 'I am in outer scope',
steps.hint: Define outerFunction with a variable declaration inside, then define innerFunction inside it. Inside innerFunction, use console.log to output both variables.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have created nested functions that demonstrate how inner functions can access variables from outer scopes through the scope chain.
successCriteria: outerFunction is defined with an 'outerVar' variable, and contains innerFunction which logs both 'outerVar' and 'innerVar'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure outerFunction declares 'outerVar', and innerFunction declares 'innerVar' and logs both variables using console.log.
steps.feedbackWrong: The scope chain example isn't complete. Create outerFunction with a variable, then define innerFunction inside it that logs both its own variable and the outer variable.

steps.instruction: creates an inner function named innerFunction that logs both 'outerVar' and its own variable 'innerVar' (with value 'I am in inner scope').
steps.hint: Define outerFunction with a variable declaration inside, then define innerFunction inside it. Inside innerFunction, use console.log to output both variables.

steps.feedbackWrong: Check the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Create a comprehensive example combining all concepts
steps.instruction: Write a complete example that demonstrates global scope, function scope, block scope, hoisting with var/let/const, and TDZ in one cohesive code block at the end of your file.
steps.hint: Create a new function called comprehensiveExample that includes examples of all the concepts you've learned. You can call existing functions and add new code inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A comprehensive function that demonstrates all scope, hoisting, and TDZ concepts together in one place.
successCriteria: The comprehensiveExample function exists and includes demonstrations of global scope, function scope, block scope, hoisting with var/let/const, and TDZ scenarios.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made progress, but your comprehensive example doesn't include all the required concepts. Make sure to demonstrate global scope, function scope, block scope, hoisting with var/let/const, and TDZ scenarios within your function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Your code doesn't include the comprehensive example as requested. Please create a function called comprehensiveExample that demonstrates all the scope, hoisting, and TDZ concepts you've learned.
